topic: An offline checklist that still works when the network doesn't

content.hook: Where is your checklist when the network is down?

slides.title: Where's your *checklist* when the network is down?
slides.body: Hint: not in a browser tab that needs Wi-Fi.

slides.title: Install it *before* you need it
slides.body: Add the web app to your home screen while online. It then works fully offline.

slides.title: Tick it off, *track progress*
slides.body: Water, food, medicine, cash, communications. See at a glance what is still missing.

slides.title: Plan for people, not only things
slides.body: Meeting point, out-of-area contact, who does what. Also available offline.

slides.title: Keep a *paper copy* too
slides.body: The planner is also a printable PDF. Paper never runs out of battery.

slides.title: A calm plan that *works offline*
slides.body: Pay what you want, from 2 PLN.

content.caption:
Offline emergency checklist: where is yours when the network is down?

If your plan lives on a website that needs a signal, it may not open when you need it most.

Ready72h has a free companion web app that installs to your home screen and works fully offline. It has an interactive checklist that tracks your progress, plus a family communication plan and a "15 minutes to leave the house" bag list. There's also a printable PDF, because paper is a good backup.

It's based on official guidance from MSB (Sweden), BBK (Germany) and RCB (Poland). Pay what you want, from 2 PLN (suggested 59 PLN). Even the minimum unlocks the full planner and app. This is a safety topic, not a place to profit off anxiety.
